en.S3Y: Song of the Three Young Men

justin: St Justin the Philosopher and Martyr

clues: I built a very big boat.
Animals came to me two by two.
After the rain, God showed me a rainbow.
I was a shepherd boy.
I played music on my harp.
With God's help, I defeated a giant with a stone.
As a baby, I was found in a basket by a river.
God spoke to me from a burning bush.
I led God's people through the Red Sea.
God asked me to go to Nineveh, but I ran away.
I was caught in a great storm at sea.
A great fish swallowed me!
I prayed to God three times every day.
The king threw me into a den of lions.
God shut the lions' mouths.
The angel Gabriel visited me.
I said yes to God.
I am the Mother of Jesus.
I was a fisherman.
I walked on the water towards Jesus.
I said three times that I did not know Jesus, but He forgave me.
I was a very short man.
I climbed a tree to see Jesus.
Jesus came to my house for dinner.
I was a bishop long ago.
I secretly gave gold to a poor family.
The Church remembers me on 6 December.
I was the very first man.
God made me from the dust of the ground.
I lived in the Garden of Eden.
I was the first woman.
I lived in a beautiful garden.
A serpent tricked me into eating the fruit.
God told me to leave my home and travel to a new land.
God said my family would be as many as the stars.
My son's name was Isaac.
I laughed when I heard I would have a baby.
I was very old when my son was born.
My husband was Abraham.
My name means laughter.
My parents were very old when I was born.
My father was Abraham.
I dreamed of a ladder reaching up to heaven.
I had twelve sons.
God gave me the new name Israel.
My father gave me a coat of many colours.
My brothers sold me, and I went to Egypt.
I explained Pharaoh's dreams.
I watched over my baby brother in a basket.
I played a timbrel and sang after crossing the sea.
My brothers were Moses and Aaron.
I was the brother of Moses.
I helped Moses speak to Pharaoh.
I became the first high priest.
I led God's people into the Promised Land.
I sent spies into Jericho.
The walls of Jericho fell down when we marched and shouted.
I said, “Where you go, I will go.”
I gathered grain in the fields of Boaz.
I became the great-grandmother of King David.
I prayed in the temple for a baby.
God answered my prayer and I had a son.
My son Samuel served God from when he was little.
I was a boy who served in God's house.
God called my name in the night.
I said, “Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.”
I was a king and the son of David.
I asked God for wisdom.
I built the great temple in Jerusalem.
Ravens brought me bread and meat.
God answered my prayer with fire from heaven.
I went up to heaven in a chariot of fire.
I was a Jewish girl who became a queen.
I bravely spoke to the king to save my people.
Maybe I was made queen for such a time as this.
I lost almost everything I had.
I kept trusting God even when I suffered.
God blessed me with twice as much in the end.
An angel found me hiding while I threshed wheat.
I asked God for a sign with a fleece of wool.
God won the battle with only 300 of my men.
God gave me great strength.
I once defeated a lion with my bare hands.
My strength was connected to my long hair.
I was a giant soldier.
I shouted at God's people every day.
A shepherd boy defeated me with a stone.
I lived in the wilderness and wore camel's hair.
I ate locusts and wild honey.
I baptised Jesus in the River Jordan.
I was the cousin of the Virgin Mary.
My baby leapt for joy when Mary visited.
My son was John the Baptist.
I was a carpenter.
An angel spoke to me in dreams.
I cared for Mary and the child Jesus.
I waited many years to see the Saviour.
I held baby Jesus in the temple.
I said, “Lord, now let your servant depart in peace.”
I was a fisherman.
I brought my brother Peter to meet Jesus.
I was the first one Jesus called to follow Him.
I used to collect taxes.
Jesus said to me, “Follow me,” and I left my table.
I wrote the first Gospel.
I was one of the twelve apostles.
I said I would not believe until I saw Jesus' wounds.
When I saw the risen Jesus, I said, “My Lord and my God!”
I used to be called Saul.
A bright light shone on me on the road to Damascus.
I travelled far and wrote many letters to the churches.
I lived in Bethany with my sisters.
I was in the tomb for four days.
Jesus called, “Come out!” and I came back to life.
I lived in Bethany with my sister and brother.
I was busy cooking when Jesus visited.
My brother was Lazarus.
I followed Jesus and helped Him.
I went to the tomb very early on Sunday.
I was the first to see the risen Jesus.
I was blind and sat by the road.
I shouted, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus healed me and I could see.
I was a teacher of the law.
I came to talk with Jesus at night.
Jesus told me about being born again.
I was one of the first deacons.
I was full of grace and power.
I was the first Christian martyr.
I was a young helper of Saint Paul.
My grandmother Lois and mother Eunice taught me the Scriptures.
Saint Paul wrote two letters to me.
I sold purple cloth.
I listened to Paul by the river.
I was baptised in Philippi with my family.
I was a brave soldier.
I would not stop following Jesus.
Icons show me on a horse defeating a dragon.
I was a shepherd before I became a bishop.
I lived on the island of Cyprus.
My holy relics rest on the island of Corfu.
I was a bishop in Caesarea.
I built a place to care for the poor and sick.
A special bread is baked for my feast on 1 January.
I was a humble bishop in Greece.
I lived on the island of Aegina.
I wrote the hymn “O Virgin Pure”.
I lived in a forest in Russia.
I fed a bear by hand.
I greeted everyone with “My joy, Christ is risen!”
I was a monk from Russia.
I travelled far across the sea to Alaska.
I cared for the children and taught them about God.
I was very clever and wise.
I explained the faith to fifty learned men.
A great monastery at Mount Sinai carries my name.
I was the mother of the emperor Constantine.
I travelled to Jerusalem.
I found the Holy Cross of Christ.
I was a Roman emperor.
I saw a cross in the sky with the words “In this sign, conquer”.
I built the city of Constantinople.
I was a doctor.
I healed the sick without asking for money.
My name means “all-merciful”.
Jesus told a story about me.
I found a hurt man lying by the road.
I bandaged him and paid for his room at an inn.
Jesus told a story about me.
I spent all my money and ended up feeding pigs.
My father ran to hug me when I came home.
I was the Roman governor.
I washed my hands in front of the crowd.
I asked Jesus, “What is truth?”
We came from the East.
We followed a bright star.
We brought gold, frankincense and myrrh.
I am an archangel.
I told Zechariah he would have a son.
I brought the good news to the Virgin Mary.
I am an archangel.
My name means “Who is like God?”
Icons show me leading the heavenly army.
The Lord filled me with His Spirit, with wisdom and skill in every kind of craft.
I was from the tribe of Judah, the son of Uri.
I made the Ark of the Covenant for the Tabernacle.
I was a prophetess who lived in Jerusalem.
My husband kept the royal wardrobe.
King Josiah's men came to ask me about the Book of the Law they had found.
I was a judge of Israel, and I was left-handed.
I made a double-edged sword about a cubit long.
I defeated Eglon, the very fat king of Moab.
I lived in a tent.
A thirsty man asked for water, and I gave him milk.
Deborah sang that I was most blessed among women, because I defeated Sisera.
I was an Ethiopian official in the king's palace.
I used old rags and ropes to rescue a prophet.
I pulled Jeremiah out of a muddy cistern.
I was a Pharisee and a teacher of the Law, honoured by all the people.
I told the council: if this work is from God, you will not be able to stop it.
Saul of Tarsus studied at my feet.
I was lame in both feet.
My nurse dropped me when I was five, as she fled in a hurry.
King David let me eat at his table always, for my father Jonathan's sake.
I lived in Joppa and was always doing good.
I made coats and clothes for the widows.
Peter prayed, and I was raised from the dead.
I sold purple cloth.
I came from the city of Thyatira.
I was baptised at Philippi and opened my home to Paul.
I was a Jew from Alexandria, eloquent and strong in the Scriptures.
Priscilla and Aquila explained the way of God to me more fully.
Paul wrote that he planted, I watered, but God gave the growth.
I was a young man in Troas.
I fell asleep while Paul talked late into the night.
I fell from a third-floor window, and Paul brought me back to life.
I was a servant girl in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark.
I was so happy to hear Peter's voice that I forgot to open the gate.
The others told me I was out of my mind.
I was a priest of Midian.
My daughter Zipporah married Moses.
I advised Moses to choose leaders to help him judge the people.
I hid a beautiful robe, silver and gold in the ground under my tent.
Because of my sin, Israel was defeated at Ai.
I lived in the time of Joshua, after the walls of Jericho fell.
I was wise and beautiful, but my husband Nabal was foolish.
I brought bread, wine, raisins and figs to David's men.
My words stopped David from taking revenge.
I was the servant of the prophet Elisha.
I ran after Naaman and lied to get silver and clothes.
Naaman's leprosy came upon me.
I was in charge of King Ahab's palace, and I feared the Lord greatly.
I hid one hundred prophets in two caves.
I fed them bread and water while Jezebel was killing the prophets.
I was a rich man and a member of the council.
I was waiting for the Kingdom of God, and I did not agree with what the council did.
I asked Pilate for the body of Jesus and laid it in my own new tomb.
The Holy Spirit told me I would not die before I had seen the Lord's Christ.
I took the baby Jesus in my arms in the Temple.
I prayed: Lord, now let Your servant depart in peace.
I was a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher.
I was very old and never left the Temple, worshipping with fasting and prayer night and day.
I gave thanks to God and spoke about the baby Jesus to everyone.
I was a disciple living in Damascus.
The Lord told me to go to a street called Straight.
I laid my hands on Saul, and he could see again.
I was a centurion of the Italian Regiment in Caesarea.
An angel told me to send for Simon Peter.
My household and I were among the first Gentiles to receive the Holy Spirit and be baptised.
My name means son of encouragement.
I sold a field and brought the money to the apostles.
I travelled with Paul on his first missionary journey.
My father Enoch walked with God.
My grandson was Noah.
I lived longer than anyone else in the Bible: 969 years.
I was from the tribe of Levi.
I hid my baby son for three months.
I made a basket of papyrus and laid my son in it among the reeds of the Nile.
I was a wealthy man of Bethlehem.
I told my workers to leave extra grain for a young widow from Moab.
I married Ruth and became the great-grandfather of King David.
Every year I went up to Shiloh and prayed for a son.
Eli the priest thought I was drunk, because my lips moved without a sound.
I gave my son Samuel to serve the Lord.
I became king when I was only eight years old.
In my reign the Book of the Law was found in the Temple.
When I heard its words I tore my clothes and led the people back to God.
I prayed when Sennacherib threatened Jerusalem.
God added fifteen years to my life.
As a sign for me, the shadow went back ten steps on the stairway of Ahaz.
I served the church at Cenchreae.
Paul asked the Christians in Rome to welcome me in the Lord.
Paul said I had been a helper of many, and of him too.
I was a leader among the brothers in Jerusalem.
I was beaten and put in prison with Paul at Philippi.
At midnight we sang hymns, and an earthquake opened the prison doors.
I was one of the twelve spies sent into Canaan.
I said: let us go up at once and take the land, for we are well able.
At eighty-five I asked for the hill country of Hebron.
I was commander of the army of the king of Aram.
A little servant girl from Israel told my wife about a prophet.
I washed seven times in the Jordan and was healed of leprosy.
I became king of Judah at sixteen and was famous for my towers and machines.
I grew proud and went into the Temple to burn incense, which only priests may do.
Leprosy broke out on my forehead in front of the priests.
I was a Hebrew midwife in Egypt.
Pharaoh told me to let the Hebrew baby boys die, but I feared God.
God was kind to me and gave me a family of my own.
